Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-boost-transcribe-medium-0012", "row_sha256": "0a4cd10be1a7cfb205a91fc364e64f3770151252960ea7f8dd7328b224994a58", "mode": "/transcribe", "language": "en", "context": {"dictionary": ["TideBoard"]}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Remove true hesitation and accidental restarts. Apply explicit corrections to the final stated intent. Preserve meaningful filler-like words and unfinished thoughts. Apply clearly spoken punctuation and list cues. Keep the supplied language.", "input": "i went to the equipment room after last period to return the class set from the science lab and the desk attendant asked if i had checked every item against the sheet yeah i said that matches the list i counted twelve tablets twelve charging cables and the blue carrying case the first tablet had a small crack already noted on the checkout form and i showed her the photo i took before class she checked the serial number and said it was the same one i had signed for i uh left the charger pouch in my locker for a second and had to go back upstairs but i brought it down before the room closed the return slip had the date as tuesday no wednesday because our school calendar had the staff day marked in the wrong place on my copy she corrected the date and gave me the yellow receipt i asked whether the stylus was supposed to stay with the tablet or go back in the pouch she said it belonged in the pouch so i put it beside the other eleven and we checked them once more the TideBoard screen was off and the case was dry she said the return was recorded and told me to keep the receipt until the teacher checked the set next morning", "output": "I went to the equipment room after last period to return the class set from the science lab, and the desk attendant asked if I had checked every item against the sheet. “Yeah,” I said, “that matches the list.” I counted twelve tablets, twelve charging cables, and the blue carrying case. The first tablet had a small crack already noted on the checkout form, and I showed her the photo I took before class. She checked the serial number and said it was the same one I had signed for. I left the charger pouch in my locker for a second and had to go back upstairs, but I brought it down before the room closed. The return slip had the date as Tuesday—no, Wednesday—because our school calendar had the staff day marked in the wrong place on my copy. She corrected the date and gave me the yellow receipt. I asked whether the stylus was supposed to stay with the tablet or go back in the pouch. She said it belonged in the pouch, so I put it beside the other eleven, and we checked them once more. The TideBoard screen was off, and the case was dry. She said the return was recorded and told me to keep the receipt until the teacher checked the set next morning."}]
